arxiv-2109-01114.title: Modular knots, automorphic forms, and the Rademacher symbols for triangle groups
arxiv-2109-01114.creator: Toshiki Matsusaka, Jun Ueki
arxiv-2109-01114.description: Abstract . É. Ghys proved that the linking numbers of modular knots and the “missing” trefoil K 2 , 3 K_{2,3} in S 3 S^{3} coincide with the values of a highly ubiquitous function called the Rademacher symbol for SL 2 ⁡ ℤ \SL_{2}\mathbb{Z} .

arxiv-2111-13886.title: Two unique Identifiability results for inverse scattering problems within polyhedral geometries
arxiv-2111-13886.creator: Xinlin Cao, Huaian Diao, Hongyu Liu, Jun Zou
arxiv-2111-13886.description: Abstract . We consider the unique determinations of impenetrable obstacles or diffraction grating profiles in ℝ 3 \mathbb{R}^{3} by a single far-field measurement within polyhedral geometries. We are particularly interested in the case that the scattering objects are of impedance type. We derive two new unique identifiability results for the inverse scattering problem in the aforementioned two challenging setups.

arxiv-2212-03757.title: Search for planets around stars with wide brown dwarfs
arxiv-2212-03757.creator: J. Šubjak, N. Lodieu, P. Kabáth, H. M. J. Boffin, G. Nowak, F. Grundahl, V. J. S. Béjar, M. R. Zapatero Osorio, V. Antoci
arxiv-2212-03757.description: Abstract Aims. The project aims to understand better the role of wide brown dwarf companions on planetary systems. Methods. We obtained high-resolution spectra of six bright stars with co-moving wide substellar companions with the SONG, CARMENES, and STELLA high-resolution spectrographs. We used these spectra to derive radial velocities together with a complete set of stellar physical parameters.

arxiv-2212-06831.title: On Almost Orthogonal Series Thanks: This work is supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China, grant No. 11771355.
arxiv-2212-06831.creator: Ruiming Zhang
arxiv-2212-06831.description: Abstract . In this work we prove analogues of Bessel inequality and Riesz-Fisher theorem in Hilbert spaces with respect to sequences. We apply our generalized Bessel inequality to the Hilbert spaces associated with the Normal, Beta, Gamma and certain discrete probability distributions to show how to generate certain type of inequalities for special functions systematically.

arxiv-2404-14178.title: Non-trivial r r -wise agreeing families
arxiv-2404-14178.creator: Peter Frankl, Andrey Kupavskii
arxiv-2404-14178.description: Abstract A family of subsets of [ n ] [n] is r r -wise agreeing if for any r r sets from the family there is an element x x that is either contained in all or contained in none of the r r sets. The study of such families is motivated by questions in discrete optimization.

arxiv-2406-11719.title: Exploring wormhole solutions with global monopole charge in the context of f ⁡ ( Q ) f(Q) gravity
arxiv-2406-11719.creator: Moreshwar Tayde, P.K. Sahoo
arxiv-2406-11719.description: Abstract This study explores the potential existence of traversable wormholes influenced by a global monopole charge within the f ⁡ ( Q ) f(Q) gravity framework. To elucidate the characteristics of these wormholes, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of wormhole solutions employing three different forms of redshift function under a linear f ⁡ ( Q ) f(Q) model.

arxiv-2502-20659.title: Low Dimensional Homology of the Yang-Baxter Operators Yielding the HOMFLYPT Polynomial
arxiv-2502-20659.creator: Anthony Christiana, Ben Clingenpeel, Huizheng Guo, Jinseok Oh, Józef H. Przytycki, Xiao Wang, Hongdae Yun
arxiv-2502-20659.description: Abstract . In this paper, we analyze the homology of the Yang-Baxter Operators R ( m ) R_{(m)} yielding the HOMFLYPT polynomial, reducing the computation of the n n -th homology of R ( m ) R_{(m)} for arbitrary m m to the computation of n + 1 n+1 initial conditions.

arxiv-2602-09936.title: The Catastrophic Failure of the k k -Means Algorithm in High Dimensions, and How Hartigan’s Algorithm Avoids It
arxiv-2602-09936.creator: Roy R. Lederman, David Silva-Sánchez, Ziling Chen, Gilles Mordant, Amnon Balanov, Tamir Bendory
arxiv-2602-09936.description: Abstract Lloyd’s k k -means algorithm is one of the most widely used clustering methods. We prove that in high-dimensional, high-noise settings, the algorithm exhibits catastrophic failure: with high probability, essentially every partition of the data is a fixed point. Consequently, Lloyd’s algorithm simply returns its initial partition — even when the underlying clusters are trivially recoverable by other methods.

pmc-10625576.title: Radiomics as a non-invasive adjunct to Chest CT in distinguishing benign and malignant lung nodules
pmc-10625576.creator: Minmini Selvam, Anupama Chandrasekharan, Abjasree Sadanandan, Vikas Kumar Anand, Arunan Murali, Ganapathy Krishnamurthi
pmc-10625576.description: In an observational study conducted from 2016 to 2021, we assessed the utility of radiomics in differentiating between benign and malignant lung nodules detected on computed tomography (CT) scans. Patients in whom a final diagnosis regarding the lung nodules was available according to histopathology and/or 2017 Fleischner Society guidelines were included.

pmc-10660698.title: Composite Angioimmunoblastic T-Cell Lymphoma and Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma Presenting with Distributive Shock
pmc-10660698.creator: Nisha Hariharan, Alisha Kabadi, Michelle Don, Mazen Odish, Benjamin Heyman, Massimo Breccia
pmc-10660698.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) and angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma (AITL) are two subtypes of non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL). The simultaneous occurrence of DLBCL and AITL in a composite lymphoma is very rare, and there are no established treatment regimens. We present the case of an 85-year-old male admitted to the intensive care unit with distributive shock, lymphocytosis, and lymphadenopathy, who was subsequently diagnosed with composite AITL and DLBCL, and treated with brentuximab vedotin (BV) and rituximab.

pmc-11290223.title: Self-learning neural network as a prediction model in non-invasive prenatal testing to detect fetal SNVs

pmc-11290223.description: al of cfDNA deep sequencing in expanding the testing range and accuracy of the present noninvasive prenatal screening (NIPS) service. pmc-11389499.title: CAR expression in invasive breast carcinoma and its effect on adenovirus transduction efficiency
pmc-11389499.creator: Abraham T. Phung, Jaimin R. Shah, Tao Dong, Tony Reid, Christopher Larson, Ana B. Sanchez, Bryan Oronsky, William C. Trogler, Andrew C. Kummel, Omonigho Aisagbonhi, Sarah L. Blair
pmc-11389499.description: BackgroundBreast cancer is the second leading cause of death in women, with invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC) and invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC) as the two most common forms of invasive breast cancer. While estrogen receptor positive (ER+) IDC and ILC are treated similarly, the multifocality of ILC presents challenges in detection and treatment, worsening long-term clinical outcomes in patients.

pmc-11487399.title: 50 Hz Temporal Magnetic Field Monitoring from High-Voltage Power Lines: Sensor Design and Experimental Validation
pmc-11487399.creator: Kenneth Deprez, Tom Van de Steene, Leen Verloock, Emmeric Tanghe, Liesbeth Gommé, Mart Verlaek, Michel Goethals, Karen van Campenhout, David Plets, Wout Joseph
pmc-11487399.description: A low-cost, tri-axial 50 Hz magnetic field monitoring sensor was designed, calibrated and verified. The sensor was designed using off-the-shelf components and commercially available coils. It can measure 50 Hz magnetic fields originating from high-voltage power lines from 0.08 µT to 364 µT, divided into two measurement ranges. The sensor was calibrated both on-board and in-lab.

pmc-11570462.title: Engagement in sexual healthcare and STI/HIV burden of first- and second-generation migrant and Western-born female sex workers in the Netherlands: A retrospective cohort study
pmc-11570462.creator: CMM Peters, YJ Evers, CJG Kampman, MJ Theunissen–Lamers, MAM van den Elshout, NHTM Dukers-Muijrers, CJPA Hoebe
pmc-11570462.description: Highlights•Largest cohort study examining migrant FSW STI burden and healthcare engagement.•Migrant FSW have higher burden and odds of infectious syphilis, hepatitis B, and HIV.•Western-born FSW have higher burden of CT and NG than first-generation FSW.•First-generation migrants less likely to have a repeat consultation versus Western-born.•Targeted outreach needed in STI clinics to improve migrant FSW healthcare retention.

pmc-11919188.title: High Blood Pressure and Depression Among the Working Population of Ghana: A Generalized Linear Model of the Risk Factors
pmc-11919188.creator: Michael Arthur Ofori, David Kwamena Mensah, Ildephonse Nizeyimana, Niharika Jha, Zebunnesa Zeba, Shongkour Roy
pmc-11919188.description: Background. The global presence of high blood pressure and depression poses a significant public health threat, particularly in emerging nations. High blood pressure and depression are inevitable among the working population of Ghana, and it is crucial to recognize the potential influence of these conditions on the working-age population. Materials and Methods.

pmc-12822186.title: The ARUTIS Study (Anglia Ruskin University Trial of the Intuitive System): a single-centre, double-masked randomised controlled crossover trial of precision tinted lenses for visual stress: study protocol for a randomised controlled trial
pmc-12822186.creator: Zahra N Ramsahye, Peter M Allen, Nikita J Thomas, Arnold J Wilkins, Bruce J W Evans, James M Gilchrist
pmc-12822186.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundVisual stress (VS), a condition affecting approximately 20% of children with reading difficulties that is alleviated with individually prescribed coloured filters, remains controversial. The purpose of the Anglia Ruskin University Trial of the Intuitive System (ARUTIS) is to investigate the effect of wearing precision tinted lenses (PTL) prescribed by the Intuitive System (IS) in children with VS using a double-masked crossover design.MethodsA total of 120 participants aged 9–18 years meeting diagnostic criteria for VS will be recruited from the Anglia Ruskin University

pmc-13118167.title: Study of the Relation Between the Reynolds Number and the Formation of Au and Ag Nanostructures by Flow-Driven Surface Modification in Microfluidic Reactors
pmc-13118167.creator: Oscar Perez-Landeros, Alan Garcia-Gallegos, David Mateos-Anzaldo, Roumen Nedev, Judith Paz-Delgadillo, Mariela Dominguez-Osuna, Evelyn Magaña-Leyva, Ricardo Salinas-Martinez, Mario Curiel-Alvarez
pmc-13118167.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Microfluidics enables spatially controlled nanostructure synthesis by coupling confined flows with surface reactions. In this work, we study how geometry-induced laminar microenvironments govern the in situ formation of Au and Ag nanostructures inside 3D-printed microfluidic reactors. Proof-of-concept fish-scale valves were fabricated by masked stereolithography in three architectures designed to define three recurring zones in the microreactor, inside the fish-scales (zone 1), between the fish-scales (zone 2), and along the rows of fish-scales (zone 3).

pmc-13120274.title: Dynamic Field Assessment of Hip Adductor Function Using a Smartphone-Based Copenhagen Test: Reliability and Concurrent Associations with Isometric Strength in Amateur Football Players
pmc-13120274.creator: Aaron Miralles-Iborra, Tomas Urban, Javier De Los Ríos-Calonge, Jose L. L. Elvira, Juan Del Coso, María Isabel Tomás-Rodríguez, Casto Juan-Recio, Víctor Moreno-Pérez
pmc-13120274.description: Assessing hip adductor muscle strength is important for identifying weakness or side-to-side imbalances associated with groin injury risk. Although the Copenhagen adductor exercise is widely used to evaluate adductor function, the quantification of strength-related outcomes using inertial sensors integrated in smartphones during this task has not been systematically examined.

pmc-13151227.title: Bayesian multilevel analysis of multimorbidity among women in Somalia: prevalence, patterns, and determinants
pmc-13151227.creator: Jama Mohamed, Ahmed Ibrahim Farah, Ahmed Ismail Mohamed, Azizur Rahman, Saralees Nadarajah
pmc-13151227.description: BackgroundMultimorbidity is a growing public health concern globally, yet remains under-researched in fragile and conflict-affected settings, including Somalia, a country in the Horn of Africa with limited health infrastructure. This study investigates the prevalence, regional patterns, and individual- and contextual-level determinants of multimorbidity among women aged 15–49 years in Somalia.

pmc-13623021.title: A scalable and cost-effective nanopore workflow for 16S rRNA microbiome profiling validated in a zebrafish gut model
pmc-13623021.creator: Maria Juanpere-Borras, Jos Boekhorst, Peter van Baarlen, Sylvia Brugman, Adrià López Nadal
pmc-13623021.description: Graphical Abstract Impact Statement High-throughput microbiome profiling remains constrained by sequencing costs, infrastructure requirements and limited flexibility in multiplexing strategies. Here, we present a scalable and cost-effective PCR-based Nanopore workflow that enables accurate 16S rRNA gene profiling using both amplicon sequence variant inference for short-read amplicons and OTU clustering for full-length sequencing.
